subject: Cloud Computing
title: Building a Culture of Resilience
description: Learn Building a Culture of Resilience in one minute.

hook.text: Companies that handle outages well share one thing: they don't punish failure. They study it and improve.

buildup.text: A resilience culture includes blameless post-mortems, regular game days, on-call training, and SLO-driven decisions.

discovery.text: Google's SRE handbook, Netflix's chaos practices, and AWS's Well-Architected reviews are templates anyone can follow.

twist.text: Technology alone can't make you resilient. Culture determines whether tools and processes get used under pressure.

climax.text: The best cloud teams assume failure is inevitable. Pessimism about uptime breeds optimism about recovery.

punchline.text: Resilience is a culture, not a tool. Build both.

quiz.question: What is the foundation of a resilient engineering culture?
options: Blameless post-mortems and treating failures as learning opportunities
Punishing engineers who cause outages to deter future mistakes
Avoiding all changes to production systems to prevent failures

details.summary: A culture of resilience accepts that failures are inevitable and builds systems, processes, and teams that recover quickly. It combines chaos testing, blameless post-mortems, well-tested runbooks, on-call rotations, and continuous investment in reliability engineering.
details.whyItMatters: Technology alone cannot prevent outages. A resilience culture ensures that when failures happen, the organization responds effectively and continuously improves.
takeaways: Resilience culture accepts that all systems eventually fail
It combines technical and organizational practices
Continuous improvement through post-mortems drives progress

faq.question: How do you build a culture of resilience?
faq.answer: Invest in reliability engineering roles, conduct regular chaos experiments, hold blameless post-mortems for every incident, maintain tested runbooks, practice incident response through game days, and measure reliability with SLIs and SLOs that the entire organization tracks.

faq.question: What is site reliability engineering?
faq.answer: SRE, pioneered by Google, applies software engineering to operations problems. SRE teams use error budgets, SLOs, and automation to balance feature development with reliability. They ensure that systems are reliable enough to meet user expectations without over-investing in perfection.
